analysis.title: Multi-Asset Strategy Daily
key_insights: Equities are driving rates. Yesterday's sharp equity reversal pulled 10Y UST yields back through 5.05%, and the move extended overnight to about 5.01%.
US equity futures are lower again, S&P futures about -0.7% and Nasdaq futures about -1.3%, after yesterday's sell-off broadened well beyond tech.

Oil is not adding pressure to rates. Brent is steady around $92.5-93pb despite a worse Hormuz security backdrop and faster Iranian attacks on shipping this month. Expectations of a global surplus and a breakdown of oil's beta to rates have kept the risk premium from rebuilding.

Mizuho takes its cue from equities today. 5% is the key level in 10Y USTs and it would not fade a break below it if the risk-asset sell-off accelerates. It still expects the back end to lead initially.
The Fed has given little indication that weaker risk assets alone will change its reaction function. Front-end supply next week should limit the scope for a larger front-end rally.

Eurozone rates are opening better bid after yesterday's sell-off. Yesterday's move brought almost three additional ECB hikes back into the curve by end-2027, which should keep the front end sticky even if duration rallies.
Mizuho sees the risk-off move as cleaner further out the EUR curve. The 10Y Bund should find support if UST 10s make a sustained move through 5%.
Mizuho is hesitant to accept the current ECB rate path priced by markets, because negotiated wage data has not shown a major acceleration.

UK October retail sales excluding autos rose 0.9% MoM vs 0.1% consensus, and public borrowing came in lower than expected with favourable September revisions. Mizuho doubts one print changes the MPC's view but sees a resilient consumer.
Better UK borrowing numbers offer relative support to the long end of the Gilt curve, while the stronger retail print can leave front-end GBP rates underperforming peers.
Asian equities sold off as the AI trade unwound further. JGB yields fell, led by the 5-7Y bucket, helped by softer CPI data. USD/JPY moved away from 160 to about 159.20.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Broad-based strength points to a resilient consumer. One print is unlikely to change the MPC's view, and it may leave front-end GBP rates underperforming.
